title: A swipe card stores data in a strip of magnetic tape
body: In the early 1960s IBM engineer Forrest Parry developed a way to attach magnetic tape to a plastic card. Tiny magnetic particles in the strip can hold a pattern that a reader picks up as the card moves past it.
takeaway: A pocket-sized card can carry data without a battery or moving parts of its own.
visual: a plain plastic card with a dark magnetic strip passing through a reader slot

title: Punched paper cards once controlled woven patterns
body: A Jacquard loom uses a chain of punched cards to control which threads rise for each pass across the loom. A hole or solid spot changes which threads the mechanism lifts.
takeaway: Changing the set of cards lets the same machine weave a different pattern.
source: Computer History Museum, Jacquard Loom and Punched Cards
visual: a chain of punched loom cards curling above taut threads
